title: tldr-read-enforcer fires on EVERY Read >3KB (30s ceiling) and uses the TLDR daemon (in-process TCP) so cold-`tldr`-CLI is amortized — BUT the Windows reachability probe + queryDaemonSync spawn a per-Read subprocess (node -e probe; PowerShell socket bridge) even on the daemon-hit path
observe_how: On Windows, each Read >3KB triggers tldr-read-enforcer -> queryDaemonSync, which calls isDaemonReachable() (spawnSync node -e TCP probe) then a PowerShell New-Object TcpClient for the actual query. Time a Read on a 5KB code file; the wall cost is ~2 child-process spawns even when the daemon is warm. The daemon removes tldr CLI cold-start but Windows reintroduces per-call process spawns.

title: railway-cli and neonctl registered as top-level JSON keys outside the skills map, in a non-schema shape — registrations are dead despite status 'verified'

evidence.quote:
"score": 90,
    "status": "verified"
for (const [skillName, config] of Object.entries(rules.skills)) {

observe_how: skill-rules.json top-level keys are [version, description, skills, agents, patterns, notes, railway-cli, neonctl] — the last two sit AFTER the notes block (lines 2909 and 2922), outside skills{}. They also use a flat {keywords, score, status} shape with no promptTriggers wrapper, so even if moved under skills they would be skipped by the hook's `if (!triggers) continue` (line 401). Net effect: zero prompt-trigger routing for two actively-documented CLI skills (both have rules: railway-deploy.md, neonctl-safety.md) while the registry claims status 'verified' / score 90 — a false routing claim that would survive any audit reading only the status fields. Fix: move both under skills{} in the promptTriggers schema; find and fix the registrar/vetting step that appended them at root.
telemetry: Skill-activation suggestion count for railway-cli/neonctl on prompts containing 'railway deploy' or 'neonctl' (currently structurally 0).

title: Fourth presentation skill family carries ~46MB across 3 overlapping skills, including a bit-identical 6.2MB brand PDF in two skills and a redundant 5.6MB zip of the skill inside itself

evidence.quote: description: Expert guidance for creating Fourth-branded PowerPoint presentations (PPTX files only) using official brand guidelines, templates, colors, typography, and layout principles. Ensures professional, on-brand presentations every time.

Phase 2 converts the approved HTML to PPTX for distribution. HTML is always built first -- PPTX is never built until the user explicitly approves the HTML design. description: Expert guidance for creating Fourth-branded content across all formats (excluding PowerPoint). Covers brand voice, messaging, visual identity, Fourth iQ branding, tone principles, color systems, typography, and photography for marketing materials, documents, web content, and all communications.

observe_how: du -sk: fourth-presentation-builder 22.8MB, fourth-presentation-suite 12.0MB, fourth-brand-guidelines 11.6MB (~46MB total — by far the heaviest skills in the tree). md5sum confirms 'fourth-presentation-builder/references/Fourth Brand guidelines.pdf' and 'fourth-brand-guidelines/references/Fourth Brand guidelines.pdf' are bit-identical (e1cd86add850965da2c9d40fba80c331, 6,208,470 bytes each). fourth-brand-guidelines additionally stores fourth-brand-guidelines.zip (5,620,402 bytes) — a packaging artifact of itself. Functionally, the suite's two-phase workflow (HTML then PPTX, with its own Fourth_2025_Template.pptx) covers the builder's PPTX-only role, and only the suite is registered in skill-rules.json; the builder (last commit 2026-03-07, referenced only by fourth-brand-guidelines) plus its 2 PPTX/POTX templates duplicates that capability. All ~46MB rides every repo->~/.claude sync and the git history. Simplify: single shared assets/references dir (or keep the PDF in one skill and cross-reference), delete the self-zip, and fold/retire the builder into the suite.
telemetry: Repo size of .claude/skills/ (currently dominated by these 3 dirs); sync-to-active.sh copy volume.
